items.title: One Nation, One Election: Supreme Court says no parliamentary panel meeting with CJI, judges
items.summary: The Supreme Court of India has said that no meeting will take place between its judges and the Joint Parliamentary Committee (JPC) examining the 'One Nation, One Election' bills. Sources at the Supreme Court revealed the same to Bar & Bench hours after Senior Advocate Kapil Sibal said at a press conference that the JPC was scheduled to hold discussions with the Chief Justice of India (CJI) and other apex court judges on October 6. According to PTI , the JPC dropped the plan to meet top court judges after the opposition raised objections to the same. The JPC, chaired by BJP Member of Parliament PP Chaudhary, is examining the Constitution (One Hundred and Twenty-Ninth Amendment) Bill, 2024 and the Union Territories Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2024. The two bills seek to put in place a framework for holding Lok Sabha and State Assembly elections together. Senior Advocate Kapil Sibal Sibal termed the proposed interaction unprecedented and unconstitutional. He said that a parliamentary committee briefing sitting judges on a bill, even before finalising its report, has never happened in India's history. He added that this goes against the principle of separation of powers among the executive, the legislature and the judiciary. Parliament makes laws and the judiciary tests their validity, he pointed out. If the amendments are passed, the same judges could be called upon to decide challenges to them. "This is a joke on the Constitution," Sibal said. The JPC has so far held consultations with political parties, legislators, constitutional experts and other stakeholders. It disclosed that it also consulted former Chief Justices of India and retired Supreme Court judges on the constitutional implications of simultaneous elections. Sibal's objection, however, was to an interaction with sitting judges, who could eventually sit in judgment over the constitutionality of the law. The bills require amendments to the Constitution and have sparked debate on federalism, the tenure of legislatures, premature dissolution of Houses and the basic structure of the Constitution.

items.title: CIRP under IBC can continue even if insolvency plea that triggered it was fraudulent: Supreme Court
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Wednesday held that a corporate insolvency resolution process (CIRP) under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code (IBC) can continue even if the insolvency application that originally triggered the process is subsequently found to have been fraudulent and collusive [Orris Vs Rakesh Kumar Gupta]. A Bench of Justices PS Narasimha and Alok Aradhe held that while the National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT) has the power to recall the admission of an insolvency application obtained through fraud, such a finding does not automatically require the entire CIRP to be terminated. “ The initiating creditor is merely the triggering creditor, and not the proprietor of the CIRP, ” the judgment said. Once an insolvency application is admitted, the proceedings cease to remain a dispute between the creditor who initiated the process and the corporate debtor. They become proceedings in rem involving the entire body of creditors and other stakeholders, the Court explained. “ The resolution process can therefore continue even in the absence of the original applicant, ” the top court made it clear. Justice PS Narasimha and Justice Alok Aradhe The Court was dealing with insolvency proceedings against Three C Shelters Private Limited, developer of the Greenopolis residential project in Gurugram. The CIRP was initiated in 2020 on a Section 9 application filed by Straight Edge Contracts Private Limited, which claimed nearly ₹30 crore as operational debt. However, the NCLT subsequently found that the insolvency proceedings had been initiated through fraud and collusion between Straight Edge and the corporate debtor. Among other things, it found that two persons who had represented Three C Shelters as directors and admitted the alleged liability were, in fact, described as an office boy and pantry boy who were unaware of the company's affairs. The NCLT also found discrepancies in documents relied upon to establish the purported operational debt. Hence, it set aside the CIRP. The decision was upheld by the NCLAT. This led to the appeal before the Supreme Court. The apex court affirmed the findings of fraud and collusion, observing that the supposed debt was a "mirage" and had been projected to enable initiation of CIRP and the consequent moratorium, thereby blocking remedies available to homebuyers and other claimants. By way of a judgment delivered on September 32, a Bench of Chief Justice Devendra Kumar Upadhyaya and Justice Tejas Karia dismissed an appeal by CCI Deputy Director (Law) Vijay Bishnoi and directed completion of the inquiry and passage of a final disciplinary order within six months. The Court left the question of whether Bishnoi had tampered with the statements to the inquiry authority. “ The charge concerns the manner in which the statements of Mr. Swaminathan and Mr. Parthasarathy came to be recorded and signed; whether the charge is established is a matter of evidence to be determined by the Inquiring Authority, ” the Court said. items.title: The Act notification veto: When 'when' quietly becomes 'never'
items.summary: Once a bill gets the President's assent, most people assume that's the end of the story. Fewer stop to ask the second question: when does it actually start applying? For at least 3 Indian statutes, no one has given a real answer to that in years. In one case, it's been more than 3 decades. Take the Delhi Rent Act. The President assented to it on August 23, 1995, but it has remained uncommenced ever since. This is because the decision on this lies with a Central government notification under Section 1(3) , which has not been made in over three decades now. Advocate Shobha Aggarwal took the matter to court in 2025 . A law that never lived Parliament passed the Act. It was signed by the President; then it lay there, as nothing in the statute obliged the government to justify itself in any time frame. The Delhi Rent Act, 1995 is, therefore, now an Act that is on the statute book but not implemented to this day, waiting for a notification “on such date as the Central government may appoint.” And this is not an isolated incident. Another example of such a law is the National Environment Tribunal Act, 1995 , which met the same fate and was finally done away with by Parliament through a new National Green Tribunal Act in 2010 . There is also the Whistleblowers Protection Act of 2014 , which became law on May 9, 2014 and has never been operational. According to a December 2025 parliamentary reply , the Act must be changed so that disclosures do not threaten India’s sovereignty and security. The Amendment Bill, introduced in 2015, passed the Lok Sabha that year but could not reach the Rajya Sabha before the 16th Lok Sabha was dissolved in 2019. This pattern repeats across the 3 statutes: Parliament passes the Act the President signs the Act and the executive simply forgets to enforce the Act. What I refer to as a “notification veto” is not a legal theory, but merely a description of the constitutional impact of the failure to commence legislation. The Court remarked that while the ECI’s protocol successfully purges non-resident entries, it fails to achieve its corresponding goal of enumerating shifted voters. The Bench also noted that rejection orders cited "system glitches," indicating the portal gave officers no choice but to reject form 8 filings. The Court also took exception to the ECI invoking public perception and confidence in the electoral exercise to support the commission's revision framework. The Bench rebuked the ECI and made it clear that court proceedings are governed strictly by legal provisions rather than external opinion and public sentiment should not be a ground to bypass the law. “What the public thinks about all of us is immaterial. items.title: Bombay High Court orders takedown of AI deepfakes, derogatory content against Samantha Ruth Prabhu
items.summary: The Bombay High Court today ordered the takedown of content found misusing the name, image and voice of actress Samantha Ruth Prabhu [ Samantha Ruth Prabhu v. John Doe & Ors ]. Justice Madhav Jamdar passed the interim order on a plea filed by Prabhu seeking the protection of her personality rights. The Court has restrained the publication of objectionable content that involve the unauthorised use of the name, image, and voice of the actress, including deepfakes created through the use of artificial intelligence. The Court passed the order after noting that the content flagged by Prabhu in her personality rights suit - including morphed content and deepfakes - demonstrated a prima facie violation of the actor's personality, publicity, and moral rights. “The plaintiff's (Samantha Prabhu's) personality rights and publicity rights are protected by Article 19(1)(a) of the Constitution of India, that is, the right to freedom of speech and expression, as also by Article 21 of the Constitution of India, that is, the right to life and personal liberty, including the right to privacy and the right to human dignity, and her moral rights as a performer are separately protected under Section 38B of the Copyright Act. Thus, all these valuable rights of the plaintiff are violated and adversely affected by the impugned actions of the defendants," the Court observed. Justice Madhav Jamdar The suit targets 18 defendants, ranging from global tech giants and AI developers to media organisations and government regulatory bodies. Named respondents include Meta Platforms (Facebook, Instagram), Google LLC (YouTube), Amazon, AI platforms and digital media outlets, apart from unidentified "John Doe / Ashok Kumar" parties. The Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) and the Department of Telecommunications (DoT) have also been made parties to the suit, so that directions can be issued to them to enforce the Court's directions in the matter. Advocate Rashmin Khandekar represented Prabhu before the Court today and highlighted widespread violations of her rights, through morphed and deepfake photographs, AI voice generation, obscene videos, and interactive AI chatbots that objectified the actress. After considering these submissions, the Court has granted Prabhu ad-interim relief by ordering the removal of such content. Advocates Anand Mohan, Lavin Hirani, Vikramaditya Chavan and Jaanvi Chopra, instructed by Hirani & Associates also appeared for Prabhu.

items.title: Supreme Court seeks West Bengal's reply on plea challenging invalidation of OBC certificates issued in 2025-26
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Thursday asked the West Bengal government to file its response to a plea challenging a Calcutta High Court ruling that declared Other Backward Class (OBC) certificates issued by the State on the strength of notifications issued in May-June 2025 invalid. A Bench of Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V Mohana today heard a batch of petitions on the issue. The petitioners' counsel today also requested the Court to stay an ongoing recruitment for constables, which could be affected by the Court's verdict in the case. The Court refused to pass any such order of stay. Instead, the Court directed that any appointments made pursuant to the recruitment would remain subject to the final outcome of the case. The High Court found that the reservation was carried out without a proper survey and that the identification of many backward classes appeared to be based on religion. According to reports , 80 of the communities were Muslim. The Court also struck down the State's sub-classification of OBCs into OBC-A (77 classes) and OBC-B (37 classes) and a provision for distributing 17 per cent reservation between the two categories. The State subsequently issued a series of notifications in May and June 2025 introducing a new OBC reservation policy. This was also challenged before the High Court. On June 17, 2025, the Calcutta High Court stayed the operation of these notifications and consequential steps. It held that the State could not use executive notifications to make changes that were inconsistent with its earlier May 2024 judgment and the statutory framework. The State government, led by then Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee of the TMC, challenged the June 2025 order before the Supreme Court. Justice Joymalya Bagchi, Justice V Mohana Representing Star Health, Senior Advocate S Muralidhar today assured the Court that the data being secured by the insurance company is secure, contrary to Pathak’s apprehensions. “ We have taken extraordinary security measures. Just because there is a dark web, we cannot be complicit,” replied Muralidhar. Senior Advocate S Muralidhar Advocate Prashant Bhushan appeared for Pathak. items.title: Kerala electricity crisis: Himachal Pradesh signs deal with KSEB, offers temporary relief
items.summary: The Congress-led government in Himachal Pradesh has come to the rescue of its counterpart in Kerala, which has been facing a major electricity crisis since it assumed power in May this year. Following negotiations with officials of Kerala State Electricity Board (KSEB), the Himachal Pradesh government has agreed to provide Kerala 600–900 MW of electricity from October 1 onwards. This is expected to be sufficient to meet the peak demand of the state. A deficient monsoon coupled with a high power consumption had disrupted KSEB’s power distribution from June to September. A senior officer of KSEB said that the purchase from Himachal Pradesh was enough to avoid the existing power curbs. In addition to the agreement with Himachal, KSEB has also managed to secure certain short term deals of around 450-500 MW. It is currently unclear whether KSEB will continue purchasing from Himachal Pradesh, though it is seeking an agreement to extend the arrangement for the next few months. KSEB is also relieved that the electricity it had to return as part of ‘swap’ agreement with other states ended by September 30. Under ‘swap’ deals, KSEB was expected to return during monsoon season the power it had purchased from other states at the time of peak summer. This monsoon season ended with a 28% deficiency on September 30. The increased domestic consumption caused by various factors, including high penetration of electric vehicles and increased use of air conditioners due to poor rainfall, aggravated the crisis. The state's hydroelectric power generation was around 19.23 MU as the storage in dams plummeted to 61.29%. The dams were 78.92% full during this time last year. Though the state government had promised to end the power crisis by mid-September, it continued till the end of the month. On September 30, the state recorded a peak demand of 5,459 MW. Despite purchasing power from BSES Yamuna Power Limited, Delhi (50-60 MW), Uttar Pradesh (100 MW), and Haryana (100 MW), the state recorded a shortage of 900 MW, forcing the KSEB to implement night-time power restrictions on Wednesday, September 30. The power crisis has even caused a rift within the ruling United Democratic Front with its convenor Adoor Prakash on Thursday, October 1 admitting that it caused dissatisfaction among the people towards the government. The UDF also faced a setback in the recent local body by-elections.

items.title: Form 7 deletions: CM DK Shivakumar, ministers and MLAs stage sit-in-dharna outside CEO’s office
items.summary: Karnataka Chief Minister DK Shivakumar on Thursday, October 1, staged a sit-in at the Chief Electoral Officer’s office in Bengaluru, demanding an FIR and a criminal investigation into the alleged bulk filing of Form 7 applications to delete voters from electoral rolls. Shivakumar, accompanied by several Cabinet Ministers and Congress leaders, met Chief Electoral Officer V Anbukkumar and submitted a memorandum seeking an immediate and time-bound investigation. He began the sit-in on the steps of the CEO’s office after the meeting. The Chief Minister alleged that pre-printed Form 7 applications containing voters’ names and EPIC numbers had been submitted in large numbers in several constituencies during the ongoing Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. Form 7 is used to seek deletion of a voter’s name from the electoral roll. Shivakumar alleged that the forms were being used to target voters from minority, Scheduled Caste, Scheduled Tribe and backward-class communities. He said between 50 lakh and 60 lakh additional voters could be targeted, and demanded that the Election Commission trace where the forms were printed and who supplied them In his memorandum, Shivakumar sought a constituency-wise and booth-wise investigation into unusually high numbers of Form 7 applications, particularly those filed between September 22 and 24. He cited around 3,000 applications in Belagavi North, 6,259 in Mudigere, 2,285 in Bhalki, 1,373 in Babaleshwar and 1,200 in Narasimha Raja. He also sought an investigation into the source of pre-printed voter information, including names and EPIC numbers, and whether electoral data had been accessed or used without authorisation. The memorandum called for scrutiny of people who submitted unusually large numbers of objections, their relationship with the voters concerned and applications that were returned by Booth Level Officers (BLOs). It also sought an investigation into claims of political coordination or facilitation in the filing of the applications. Shivakumar alleged that BJP and JD(S) leaders and workers were involved in the bulk submissions. He cited statements allegedly made by BJP workers and leaders acknowledging that Form 7 applications had been filed through their associates. The allegations are part of the material submitted by Shivakumar to the CEO. items.title: How HCU’s Left-Ambedkarite alliance overturned previous ABVP sweep in student polls
items.summary: The University of Hyderabad’s student union election has ended with a result that, on the surface, looks like a reversal of last year. The left-leaning AISA-ASA-DSU-SFI-TSF alliance has won all four executive positions for 2026-27, along with the cultural secretary post. The right-wing ABVP-SLVD (Akhil Bharatiya Vidyarthi Parishad – Sevalal Vidyarthi Dal) panel retained only the sports secretary post. The elections took place on September 28 and the results were declared the next day. But the result is not simply a Left-Ambedkarite victory over the ABVP. It is also the reversal of the political conditions that produced ABVP’s sweeping victory in 2025. Last year, ABVP-SLVD won all six major posts, returning to power after seven years. A major factor was the split between the Students’ Federation of India (SFI) and the Ambedkar Students’ Association (ASA), two organisations that had together helped keep ABVP out of power since 2019. The two had disagreed over the inclusion of Muslim student organisations, while the Congress-affiliated NSUI also faced student dissatisfaction over the university’s land issue, according to reporting at the time. This year, SFI and ASA were back together. The All India Students’ Association (AISA), Dalit Students’ Union (DSU) and Tribal Students Front (TSF) joined them. The result suggests that organisational arithmetic still matters enormously at HCU, even when student politics is often discussed through broader national ideological narratives. 78.1% turnout, and a near-complete alliance victory A total of 5,941 students were eligible to vote this year, of whom 4,641 cast their ballot, putting turnout at 78.1%. SFI’s Dilshada Raihan defeated ABVP-SLVD’s Naresh P for president, securing 2,178 votes against 1,727. For vice-president, TSF candidate Korra Nithin Chauhan defeated ABVP-SLVD’s Barsharani Behera by more than 200 votes. ASA’s Pratik Sagar won the general secretary post against ABVP’s Venisa Choudhary, while AISA’s Siddhant Shaswat defeated ABVP-SLVD’s Sapthagiri for joint secretary by more than 300 votes. The cultural secretary contest was the closest. ASA’s Abhinash Kumar eventually won against ABVP’s Madhur Dhingra by five votes. The announcement of that result became contentious during counting. ABVP demanded a recount, and supporters of the two sides clashed. The Election Commission withheld the announcement before the university administration subsequently declared the result.
